output.brief:
The problem is concentrated in Kestrel, not in pay or the firm-wide hours target. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, against 1 of 13 who were not on it. Other groups' attrition is flat, so ordinary market movement and the January target change don't explain it. Pay doesn't explain it either: the group sits at the same salary percentile as the rest of the firm, the rival firm's band is £3–5k higher (not £15k), and most leavers took equal or lower pay. A retention payment would cost £228k and probably wouldn't fix it. I'd advise against announcing it or closing the review.

What I can't tell is whether the cause is the workload on Kestrel or how Dorian Faulk supervises. All 11 Kestrel associates reported to him, so the records can't separate the two. The survey comments point to both. I'm moderately sure of the Kestrel link and unsure which of the two is the cause. Next step: commission the roughly £9k confidential external interviews, set up to separate supervision from workload. Start adding matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Then choose between moving supervision and adding contract reviewers. Document review runs to December 2026, so keep the interviews quick.
